notes: Early-stage SMB, consumer chat product (in-app assistant + support). Self-serve signup, trying to validate live demo before committing paid plan. Key pain: bursts during email campaigns / feature launches cause 429s; they observed concurrency limits hit on a single org key. Quotes: "We can go viral fast — need to not be blocked by quotas". Very price sensitive; wants simple rules: burst allowance, per-minute concurrency, and predictable backoff guidance. Asks about automatic retry/backoff examples and whether Redwood exposes queue/concurrency headers. Interested in hosted since no infra ops team. Has basic SOC2 ask and needs audit logs for enterprise customers later. SE Priya provided example token-cost calc and suggested Optimize settings; customer requested sample application-level throttling snippets (JS/Python) and expected behavior for 429s. Typical traffic: baseline 3 QPS, campaign spikes to ~60 QPS for 3-7 minutes; session lengths avg 120 tokens. They want to avoid user-visible failures during spikes.
use_case_summary: Customer builds an in-app conversational assistant + triage bot. Primary metrics: < 250ms token latency for chat UI, keep errors < 0.5% during sales-driven spikes, minimize extra token costs via caching/prefix reuse.
requirements_summary: Needs hosted API with predictable quotas and burst smoothing. Requests: documented default rate limits on trial keys, configurable per-key quotas for paid plans, >= short burst window (60–90s) that tolerates 3-5x baseline QPS, guidance on exponential backoff + client-side concurrency limits, example SDK snippets. Wants telemetry headers to map 429s->resource (e.g., concurrency vs overall limit). No on-prem or VPC now.
